tip: Loanwords like email do not add -s in the plural; the number shows on the adjective: molte email = many emails.
In ritardo means late or delayed, and the preposition is always in: il treno arriva in ritardo.
After dice che stating a fact, use the indicative: dice che arriva tardi, not the subjunctive.
E possibile che signals uncertainty, so the verb goes subjunctive: arrivi, not arriva.
Bravo takes a before an infinitive to mean good at doing something: bravo a cucinare.
Cercare already means to look for, so no preposition follows it: cerca le chiavi, never cerca per.
The adjective agrees with the subject's gender: a man is bravo, a woman brava, as in sei brava.
Lo and la drop their vowel to l' before a noun starting with a vowel: l'ambulanza, not la ambulanza.
Use lo, not il, before a noun starting with s plus consonant or ps: lo psicologo.
The preposition a merges with il to form al: a plus il centro becomes al centro.
Impersonal si plus a verb means a general you or one: come si arriva = how do you get there.
Volere che takes the subjunctive; in the past that is the imperfect subjunctive: volevo che tu sapessi.
Fixed time phrases like a fine anno drop the article: a fine anno, not alla fine dell'anno.
The adjective matches the noun in number: a masculine plural noun takes -i, so documentari sono educativi.
Alla plus a noun names a cooking style: alla griglia = grilled, alla romana = Roman-style.
No article before a day of the week when saying what day it is: era domenica, not era la domenica.
Abbastanza means enough, never changes form, and sits before the noun: abbastanza soldi.
Imperfetto plus da plus a time span means had been doing: cercavi da tempo = you had been looking for a while.
Fare has the irregular past participle fatto, so the passato prossimo is hai fatto, not hai fato.
Italian keeps both negatives: non before the verb plus nessuno after it together mean not anyone: non conoscevo nessuno.
Clock times use a plus le: arrivo alle otto = I arrive at eight o'clock.
Bisognava che expresses necessity and takes the imperfect subjunctive: bisognava che studiassimo.
Qualunque, meaning whatever or any, triggers the subjunctive: qualunque cosa dicesse, not diceva.
A past main verb pulls the subjunctive into the imperfect: pensavo che tu parlassi, not parli.
Prendere has the irregular past participle preso, so the passato prossimo is ho preso.
Italian uses avere, to have, for this feeling: aveva paura = was afraid, literally had fear.
Vorrei is the conditional of volere and softens a request: vorrei un caffe = I would like a coffee.
